I generally prefer we take an incremental approach to fixing APIs: Introduce a new function with a different symbol name, deprecate the existing function, switch known consumers to the new function, then remove the old one.

Why not pass the new struct (rather than separate net/eid) for this?
... or maybe this is more a question of the public API changes. Do we want to represent the (net, eid) as a common structure in the API too, or keep separate (as you have done here)?

I think given we translate into TID space, which is not currently segmented in anyway, it might be worth avoiding introducing a new type into the public API to hold these two values. I think we can keep them separate as they are now (and in the case of the caller running under linux, they can unpack them from the `struct mctp_fq_addr` instance if they have one for the purpose of the call).

I am ok either way.

Leaving the network value unset previously in `pldm_transport_af_mctp_send()` made the request use `MCTP_NET_ANY` (which is defined as net 0). Now you're unconditionally setting it to the lookup result.

Providing a result of `1` here is an unnecessary change in behaviour. I'd suggest assigning `MCTP_NET_ANY` to make it explicit.

If users have multiple networks and need to target a specific network, then they need your new APIs. Users of the existing API here should continue to have `MCTP_NET_ANY` used on send.
Done
